root_cause_hypothesis: The force-login action opens a new tab, but the admin_impersonator session key is not reliably propagated to that new browser context, causing intermittent 403s when ClarityScoutForceLoginController checks session()->has('admin_impersonator').

investigation_summary.precedent_analysis: PR #410 fixed duplicate-GET token revocation and wrong-account revocation, but did not address session availability in new tabs. Ticket filed day after PR merge suggests remaining regression.

mechanics.trigger_path: Admin Panel > Scout Users > 'Login to Scout' icon (arrow-right-on-rectangle) > Opens new tab to /scout/force-login/{kit}
mechanics.session_set_location: ImpersonateController::impersonate() lines 56-58, only for hardcoded admin IDs [1,3,10,50,25,41,35,8,45,48]
mechanics.new_tab_behavior: ScoutUsersResource.php line 354: shouldOpenInNewTab: true causes browser to open new context that may not inherit session
mechanics.token_lifecycle: PR #410 introduced ScoutForceTokens::mintFor() which keeps 3 most recent tokens per driver, tracks minted IDs in impersonator's session under 'clarity_scout_force_token_ids', revokes on impersonation exit/re-entry

primary.symptom: 403 response from ClarityScoutForceLoginController when session()->has('admin_impersonator') returns false
primary.cause: New tab opened by 'Login to Scout' action does not reliably inherit admin_impersonator session key
evidence: Action uses shouldOpenInNewTab: true which creates new browser context
Session cookies may not propagate immediately or at all depending on SameSite attribute, browser session isolation, timing
Intermittent nature matches session race condition pattern
Works then fails consecutively suggests session state desync rather than token exhaustion

secondary_considerations.session_expiry: Admin impersonation session could expire between impersonate() and force-login click, but this would be consistent failure not intermittent
secondary_considerations.cache_issue: Post-PR-410, service worker no longer caches force-login HTML (line 25-26 of commit message), so this is ruled out
secondary_considerations.token_revocation: PR #410 fixed duplicate-GET revocation by keeping 3 most recent tokens and tracking IDs in session, so this is ruled out as root cause

code_paths: ImpersonateController.php:56-58 - Hardcoded admin ID list determines who gets admin_impersonator session key

fixed: Duplicate GET token revocation (now keeps 3 most recent per driver)
Wrong-account revocation (tokens tracked in impersonator's session, not driver's)
Silent 401 client bounce (handleUnauthorized now records status/message)

ticket_context.symptom: Worked then failed for 3 Scout users consecutively
related_tickets: Guard shift side effects for force-login impersonators
Blocked lazy shift auto-start for force-login impersonators
Force-login token lifecycle / wrong-user revocation (addressed by PR #410)

unanswered_questions.q: What is the application's session driver and configuration (file, database, redis)?
unanswered_questions.why: Session propagation behavior to new tabs depends heavily on session driver and SameSite cookie settings. Database/redis sessions with strict SameSite may not propagate to new tabs opened via window.open or target=_blank.

unanswered_questions.q: Does the admin_impersonator session key have any explicit TTL or is it deleted on certain events?
unanswered_questions.why: ImpersonateController::exitAdminMode() forgets the key, but are there other paths that clear it? Could the key expire between page load and button click?

unanswered_questions.q: Can we reproduce with consecutive force-logins in rapid succession, or only after some delay?
unanswered_questions.why: If it's timing-dependent, that strengthens the race-condition hypothesis. If delay-dependent, could be session sync lag.

unanswered_questions.q: Do the 3 failed users in the demo have any common characteristics (same org, same kit configuration, etc)?
unanswered_questions.why: If they're all from one org or have specific settings, could narrow to an org-specific session or permission issue.

unanswered_questions.q: When it fails, does the user see a 403 error page or blank page or redirect?
unanswered_questions.why: Current controller aborts with 403 and message 'Forbidden', but understanding what the user actually sees helps confirm the failure path.

unanswered_questions.q: Is the force-login route protected by any middleware besides 'auth'?
unanswered_questions.why: Line 105 of web.php shows ->middleware('auth') only. No CSRF, no rate limiting. But could there be global middleware affecting session availability?

AC1_reproduce_with_active_session.approach: Impersonate as admin, verify admin_impersonator session is set, click 'Login to Scout' in new tab, observe if 403 occurs. Test with both same-tab navigation and new-tab open.

AC2_identify_root_cause.hypothesis: Session key not reliably propagated to new tab context
AC2_identify_root_cause.alternative: Could also be session cookie SameSite=Strict blocking cross-context reads

considerations: Option A: Pass admin_impersonator status via signed URL parameter instead of session check
Option B: Open force-login in same tab (no new tab) so session is guaranteed available
Option C: Add JavaScript to verify session availability before navigation, fallback to same-tab
Option D: Store admin_impersonator in more persistent storage (database flag on User) rather than session

AC4_explicit_ui_reason_when_blocked.current: Controller returns 403 with 'Forbidden' message, but this is not a friendly user-facing error
AC4_explicit_ui_reason_when_blocked.needed: Catch 403 from force-login and display user-friendly message: 'Admin session expired. Please refresh the admin panel and try again.'

AC5_product_confirm_force_login_kicks_re.current_behavior: ScoutForceTokens keeps 3 most recent tokens per driver and does NOT delete the driver's live 'clarity-scout-token'. Force tokens have separate name 'clarity-scout-force-token' and separate ability 'clarity-scout-force'. ClarityScoutAuthController::login() (line 64) deletes only 'clarity-scout-token' before minting new one.
AC5_product_confirm_force_login_kicks_re.answer: Force-login does NOT kick the real driver. Both tokens can coexist. Driver's live token remains valid unless they re-login themselves or their token expires.
AC5_product_confirm_force_login_kicks_re.product_decision_needed: Confirm this is desired behavior or if force-login should revoke driver's live session

recommended_next_steps: 1. Reproduce: Impersonate as admin, verify session, click 'Login to Scout' multiple times in new tabs. Capture 403s.
2. Inspect session config: Check config/session.php for driver, same_site, and secure settings. Check if SameSite=Strict or Lax.
3. Test session propagation: Add test that verifies admin_impersonator session key IS available in new tab context after impersonation.
4. Validate PR #410 deploy: Confirm production is running post-PR-410 code (commit 83fb68d24 or later). If not deployed, intermittent failure could still be duplicate-GET token revocation.
5. Review activity logs: Check activity_log table for 'clarity-scout-force-login' entries vs 403 failures to quantify failure rate.
6. Browser testing: Test across Chrome, Safari, Firefox to see if new-tab session behavior differs by browser.

approach_1_signed_url.description: Pass admin_impersonator verification via signed URL parameter instead of session check
pros: URL signature provides same security as session check
Works reliably across tabs and browsers
cons: Requires adding signature generation to ScoutUsersResource action
Needs to validate signature doesn't outlive impersonation session
implementation: Change ScoutUsersResource action URL to use URL::signedRoute()
Remove session()->has('admin_impersonator') check, rely on signature validation
Add timestamp to signature to expire after e.g. 60 seconds

approach_2_same_tab.description: Remove shouldOpenInNewTab: true, open force-login in same tab
cons: Admin loses their place in Scout Users table
Must navigate back to resume work
implementation: ScoutUsersResource.php line 354: remove shouldOpenInNewTab: true parameter

approach_3_session_clone.description: Add JavaScript to explicitly clone session to new tab before navigation
cons: May not work with SameSite=Strict cookies

approach_4_persistent_flag.description: Store admin_impersonator state in database on User model or separate table instead of session
pros: Most reliable, survives tab opens, refreshes, etc
Allows tracking who is currently force-logged-in
cons: Adds DB writes on every impersonation enter/exit
Must handle stale flags if impersonation exits uncleanly
implementation: Add 'is_admin_impersonator' boolean + 'admin_impersonation_started_at' timestamp to users table
Clear flag on leave() and exitAdminMode()
Add cleanup job to clear stale flags older than e.g. 8 hours

recommendation.rationale: Most robust fix that eliminates session propagation issue while preserving new-tab UX. Signed URLs are a Laravel built-in, well-tested, and provide equivalent security to session checks. The signature can be time-limited to match the scope of an admin impersonation session.
recommendation.fallback: Approach 2 (same-tab) if signed URL implementation is deemed too complex for the urgency of the fix. Worse UX but guaranteed to work.

escalate.reason: Root cause hypothesis is clear and testable. Multiple fix approaches identified with concrete implementation paths. No deep Laravel internals or architectural decisions blocking progress.

files_to_change: routes/web.php (add signed middleware if using approach 1)
blast_radius.reason: Isolated to force-login flow. No changes to normal Scout login, driver sessions, or token lifecycle. PR #410 already fixed the token revocation issues, so this is purely about admin session availability.
